Pre-fix: parser_expr.wat:295 checked (i32.const 64) for TBang, claiming
"TBang (64)" in the comment. Lexer.wat:25 declares TBang=63 (TPipe=64).
Off-by-one bug. Every `!expr` in wheel-source fell through to default-
LitUnit at parse_expr.wat:308, advancing pos by 1 (consuming the `!`)
and emitting LitUnit (which lowers to (i32.const 0) per uniform-i32 /
TUnit-as-sentinel-0).

Surfaced cascade: scan_decimal at src/lexer.mn:375 has `b == 46 &&
!is_float && pos + 1 < n && is_digit(byte_at(source, pos + 1))`. The
`!is_float` operand became (i32.const 0), making the chained predicate
`(b == 46) AND 0` always-false. The float-detection branch never
fired. Combined with how the broader if-cascade lowered, mentl2's
compiled scan_decimal infinite-recursed via lex_from → scan_number
→ scan_decimal on input containing any digit (`5\n` traps; `x\n`
doesn't). Trap: "wasm trap: call stack exhausted" (16+ recursive
frames in the backtrace).

Fix: change the comparison to (i32.const 63) — matching lexer.wat:25.
Single-character substrate fix; chunk-header documents the off-by-one
+ named follow-up history.

mentl/0975e67:
- Top-level closures emitted as static (data ...) segments at compile
  time. The graph knows every top-level fn's layout (fn_idx + 0
  captures = 8 bytes); emit projects it directly via le4-escaped data
  literals. (global $<name> i32 (i32.const <addr>)) points to the
  static record. No _init_closures runtime routine; no startup walk;
  the host populates the records during module instantiation. DESIGN
  Ch 4 "the graph IS the program" — emit projects state, doesn't
  generate code that builds it. Static closure region: 0x100..0xFFFF
  (between WASI iov scratch at 0x50–0x60 and the bump heap at 1MB).

- emit_alloc_to_local(size, target_local) factored as the swap
  surface for the future Memory handler (W5). The closure layout is
  stable; the alloc primitive becomes the swap point — bump → arena
  → gc handlers all emit different sequences without disturbing
  callers. _start drops _init_closures, calls $main directly through
  its static closure pointer.
mentl/09913ac:
Two related defensive changes in the type-driven dispatch in lower.lux:

(1) Index(coll, idx) now checks `lexpr_ty(lowered_coll)`: if TTuple,
    emit with is_tuple=true (direct i32.load offset) instead of the
    list_index call. For the actual self-hosting blocker (ctx[3] on
    polymorphic ctx), inference leaves ctx as TVar so this path
    doesn't fire — the destructuring fix in wasm_collect.lux is what
    closes the loop. But: any future code with explicit TTuple types
    accessed via [i] now lowers correctly without round-tripping
    through the list_index runtime function.

(2) BinOp Eq/Neq now checks both sides for TString. Previously only
    `lt` was matched; if the left side typed as TVar but the right
    was a string literal (the common pattern `dynamic_str == "foo"`),
    the lowerer fell through to val_eq instead of str_eq. val_eq
    works in principle but adds overhead; str_eq is the typed fast
    path. The `dynamic_str == "literal"` shape is everywhere in the
    compiler (handler-prefix detection, name lookups), so this
    matters in aggregate.

stoop/09b3684:
Seven tabs became one surface. The press, the issue as pages, is always
on screen and is home: opening stoop shows your zine, not a two-person
daily log. Everything else slides in over it from the right, one drawer
at a time, below the bar so the bar stays usable: the desk, the shelf,
the notebook and the scene. Log, journal and projects are tabs of the
notebook now, demoted from the top level to what they are, sources the
desk draws from. Settings and sync are the scene: who writes, what it is
called, where it lives, how it travels. The old hashes all still work.

Two verbs sit apart from the places. PAPER is a drawer too, holding
every paper concern in one place: the fold hand, the numbered test
sheet, SAVE PDF as the big button, browser print, the flyer, and
clearing the pages. The format stays above the pages, because changing
it changes what is on screen. HAND IT ON exports the latest published
issue as the file that is also a press, and says so and opens the desk
if nothing has been published yet.

The photo tray stopped being a mode. Arming a photograph and then
clicking a panel is gone; drop and paste are the way in, + PHOTO opens
the device's picker through the same intake as a drop, and photographs
the scene already has sit in a strip where one click glues one to the
page last touched. Clearing the pages clears the cuttings too, with undo.

The collapse did not shrink the app. It removed surface, which is HTML
and cheap, and added a router, drawers and a picker, which are not: the
press is 194 KB built, four more than before, against a ratchet of 192.
The ratchet is now derived instead of chosen. The megabyte ceiling on a
full issue, less eight photographs at about 83 KB, leaves 360 KB for the
press, rounded down to 256 KB; past that the press could reach the
ceiling on its own. The suites open the paper drawer before reaching for
a paper control, the way a person now does.
